rationale: Y's must-fix findings (ownership validation rejecting ~226 valid EngineArgs fields, the async_scheduling/scheduler_cls divergence) directly hit the architectural crux the human reviewer flagged — config parity gaps and incomplete owner sets — backed by concrete, quantified repros (81 YAMLs checked, 51 pipelines swept). X missed all seven ground-truth inline bugs and, worse, explicitly marked the two areas ground truth flags as broken (model_subdir/tokenizer_subdir precedence, omni_kv_config precedence) as 'validated' correct, actively asserting the code is fine where it isn't. Both share the same legitimate ROCm dead-code catch not in ground truth. Both are highly actionable with concrete file/line evidence, but Y's findings are better grounded and more relevant to what the human reviewer actually cared about.
